result.topic_en: Gauss expresses the lemniscatic sine of a complex argument (a+bi)ϖ as a theta-type series of sines with Gaussian factors, and rewrites it, after dividing by exponential factors, as a single sum of exponentials over odd integers k.
result.transcription:
Es sei $P\varphi = \varphi - \frac{1}{60}\varphi^5 + \&c.$
$P'(a+bi)\varpi = \sqrt{\frac{\pi}{\varpi\sqrt{2}}}\cdot\left(2e^{-\frac{1}{4}\pi}\cdot\sin(a+bi)\pi - 2e^{-\frac{9}{4}}\sin 3(a+bi)\pi + \text{etc.}\right)$
$P' = \frac{P}{e^{(\frac{1}{2}aa+abi-\frac{1}{2}bb)\pi}}$
$P'' = \frac{P}{e^{(\frac{1}{2}aa-abi+\frac{1}{2}bb)\pi}} = \frac{P'}{e^{(bb-2abi)\pi}}$
$\pm e^{-\frac{kk}{4}}\cdot e^{aki-bk} - e^{-aki+bk}$
k alle posit und neg ungeraden
$P'' = \sqrt{\frac{\pi}{\varpi\sqrt{2}}}\cdot\frac{\Sigma e^{-\frac{kk}{4}-bk+aki-bb+2abi}}{i}$

methods.what: Power series of the lemniscatic sine function
Theta-series (sine series with Gaussian weights) for a normalized lemniscatic function at complex argument
Definition of normalized functions by dividing by Gaussian exponential factors, and relation between them
Expansion of each sine term into exponentials, summing over all positive and negative odd k
Representation of P'' as a single exponential sum over odd integers k
